Lazaret
Static security, supply-chain & quality analysis · Python, JavaScript & SQL

Analyze code

Analysis runs entirely in your browser. No code leaves this page.

Issues

Lazaret performs pattern- and heuristic-based static analysis. It catches common issues but is not a substitute for a full security audit, dependency scanning, or dynamic testing.

Lazaret's native engine: notices
================================

The native engine (this directory) is Lazaret's own work, licensed under the
Apache License 2.0 (../LICENSE). It holds Unicode data (below), distributed
under the Unicode License v3 in LICENSE-UNICODE (SPDX: Unicode-3.0), so the
crates' license is Apache-2.0 AND Unicode-3.0.

The compiled engine ships in Lazaret's platform wheels and, compiled to
WebAssembly, in the npm package (as native/lazaret.wasm, this file as
native/NOTICE), each with LICENSE-UNICODE. Those packages are
Apache-2.0 AND Unicode-3.0 too. The browser dashboard
(python/src/lazaret/web/lazaret.html) carries the WebAssembly engine too,
and this file and LICENSE-UNICODE in its notices.


What was CPython's
------------------

Until P-16 (0.1.9), parts of the engine were translations into Rust of
CPython code (https://github.com/python/cpython), distributed under
CPython's license as well as Lazaret's:

    src/pyre/                    Lib/re/_parser.py, _compiler.py and
                                 _constants.py, and Modules/_sre (the SRE
                                 library, whose notices allowed its
                                 redistribution under CNRI's Python 1.6
                                 license and asked any other use to contact
                                 Secret Labs AB)
    src/hooks.rs, in part        Lib/shlex.py (shlex_split)
    src/unicode.rs, in part      Objects/unicodeobject.c
                                 (handle_capital_sigma)
    src/generated/unicode13.rs,  the table of Lib/re/_casefix.py
    in part

They are retired, and with them their notices. The engine's regular
expressions are linre (src/linre/), written from re's documented and
observed behaviour, with src/pyre.rs as re's interface to it; a command's
words are read by rules written from shlex's documentation; the Final_Sigma
rule of str.lower() follows the Unicode Standard's definition; and re's
extra case equivalences are derived from Unicode's case mappings
(scripts/make_rust_tables.py). Tests hold each to Python's own answers.


pratique
--------

Lazaret's network layer is built on pratique
(https://github.com/lazaret-dev/pratique; called tiny_https until October
2026), an HTTPS/TLS library under the Apache License 2.0
(crates/pratique/LICENSE), Lazaret's own licence. It is in crates/pratique
as it is upstream, at the commit crates/pratique/LAZARET.md names, with the
notices of what it holds from elsewhere in crates/pratique/NOTICE. The
native library holds its network part (crates/lazaret-net) and its pure
verification code (crates/lazaret-verify: the Go checksum database's check,
npm's and PyPI's attestations); the WebAssembly build holds what the engine
takes of the pure part (SHA-256, for the signed requests of live secret
verification).

Of crates/pratique/NOTICE, this is what the native library holds: the
bitsliced AES S-box and the constant-time carry-less multiplication of its
TLS code follow BearSSL (src/crypto/aes_ct.rs and src/crypto/ghash.rs in
crates/pratique), which is under the MIT licence:

Mozilla Public License 2.0, as NSS is) is for a feature Lazaret does not
use; no package of Lazaret's carries it.

Gradle's wrapper checksums
--------------------------

crates/lazaret-engine/rules/lazaret-rules.json holds, as
GRADLE_WRAPPER_CHECKSUMS, the SHA-256 of each Gradle release's wrapper jar,
as Gradle publishes them (https://services.gradle.org, each release's
wrapperChecksumUrl) and as gradle/actions lists them
(https://github.com/gradle/actions,
sources/src/wrapper-validation/wrapper-checksums.json); written by
scripts/update_gradle_wrapper_checksums.py. A checksum is a fact computed
from a file, not a work of authorship: the list is named here for where it
came from, and no licence applies to it. The rule pack is compiled into the
engine, the native library's and the WebAssembly build's alike, so both
carry the list.


Unicode data
------------

crates/lazaret-engine/src/generated/unicode13.rs holds data of the Unicode
Character Database 13.0 — the code points it assigns, the properties the
engine's regular expressions and normalization read, decompositions,
canonical combining classes and the primary composites — written by
scripts/make_rust_tables.py from Python 3.10's unicodedata. The Python
parser's table, unidata.rs in crates/lazaret-engine/src/pyparse/, holds
data of the Unicode Character Database 15.1 — the characters identifiers
may hold, normalization data of the characters assigned since 13.0, and
the character names and their aliases — written by
scripts/make_pyparse_tables.py from Python 3.13's unicodedata. And
crates/lazaret-engine/src/generated/codecs.rs holds the characters Python's
single-byte, CJK and ISO-2022 codecs decode bytes to (with the names a
coding cookie can give, facts about Python), written by
scripts/make_codec_tables.py from Python's own decoders; CPython made those
codecs' mappings for the most part from the Unicode Consortium's mapping
tables and the vendors' published ones (Microsoft's cp932, cp936, cp949 and
cp950). The archive readers' table, fold_table.rs in
crates/lazaret-archive/src/, holds data of the Unicode Character Database
15.1 — the case foldings, decompositions and canonical combining classes
the readers use to find names that a file system writes to one path,
taken from Python 3.13's unicodedata, and the Default_Ignorable_Code_Point
ranges of DerivedCoreProperties.txt, which the generator lists itself —
written by crates/lazaret-archive/tests/fixtures/generate_fold_table.py.
